clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the following year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and her joining the church choir in September 1953 as her anxiety eased.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failure in May 1968 when the late frost destroyed the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily that summer, he and Glen blamed each other and clashed, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, you began wetting the bed in April 1969, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found, and Walter stopped drinking by October 1969 and took work pruning trees.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat out of work in the truck for months, you and Glen fought loud rows over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and pulled away from your mother, your grandfather Walter drank again after six years sober, and by June 1976 you were eating again and made the track team.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Sam's mother Wilma's move into your house in January 1990: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, Sam worked late and kept out of the rows, Sam took his mother's side, your son Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over your daughter Lily's care, you broke out in eczema on both hands, you and Sam rowed most nights, and your mother drove over twice a week to take your side; by June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town and your eczema cleared over the summer.
